newsitem.title: JAPAN: DDI 96/97 profit seen larger than forecast - paper.
newsitem.headline: DDI 96/97 profit seen larger than forecast - paper.

text.p: DDI Corp's parent current profit is expected to be 67 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1997, larger than the company's November forecast of 60 billion yen, a Japanese business daily said on Tuesday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said its larger estimate was due to a cut in fees the company pays to Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT).
A DDI spokesman said, however, that it had not agreed with NTT on the access charges it pays to NTT for use of NTT facilities. He declined to comment on the newspaper report.
DDI is one of Japan's long-distance domestic telecommunications operators.
DDI posted a parent current profit of 57.69 billion yen in 1995/96.
Nihon Keizai said on Sunday that NTT would cut its access fees by 12 percent.
The paper said the new rates would be retroactively applied to long-distance telecommunications companies from April 1996.
